# Independent audit: small mass outside a complete parity core

Audited `candidate ff31d56304dd901a` line by
line, including the repaired current formatting. **PASS; no
mathematical correction needed.** I also reran
`supporting computation verify_arbitrary_simplex_parity_core_credits.py`, which passes its
exact simplex and arbitrary-transversal calibrations. That verifier
does not replace the written compactness proof for arbitrary shapes.

## Uniformity over an arbitrary finite star

Maximum-inscribed-simplex normalization gives the claimed common
bounded class: replacing a vertex bounds every barycentric coordinate
in absolute value by one. The normalized body contains the fixed
simplex and remains in the fixed cube. A limit with ordinary maximum
depth Gamma must be a simplex by the independently proved rigidity
theorem. Since the fixed simplex remains maximum-volume inscribed,
the limiting simplex is exactly that fixed simplex. This proves
uniform convergence over the entire class of normalized near-minimal
bodies, without fixing any number of pairs.

The opposite translations of one pair are legitimate identities for
the arbitrary paired thresholds. They preserve the middle body and
midpoint inclusion. They put the partner in twice the middle body
and the small source in twice its difference body, so all bodies used
in that pair calculation have the stated common radius bound. A
near-equal-volume partner has a full-dimensional compact limit; its
near-minimal ordinary depth forces a simplex limit. Consequently its
maximum inscribed simplex has volume uniformly close to the middle
volume. A failure of uniformity over arbitrarily many pairs would
select one offending pair at each parameter value and contradict
this same compactness argument. No common ambient shear of all
pairs is asserted or needed.

For the determinant step, q=N-J+1 exceeds N/2. Replacing the first
row by the sum of all rows and centering the remaining rows gives
the stated Hadamard bound. All the omitted row maxima are at most
one, and the final q maxima are at most the J-th largest. The volume
ratio in (10) therefore implies the row threshold b+delta exactly.
Conversion from outer-simplex barycentrics to the fixed ones has
the correct direction because its dilation factor is at least one.
This proves at least J high-coordinate credits at every point of
each small source, without requiring that the selected coordinates
remain constant across that source.

The homothetic partner-cap argument works for every real tilt.
For small enough theta, every source/partner root ratio is below
one, so the homothetic copy really lies in the partner. If the
partner cap fails to pay the whole small-source mass, the small
source threshold is strictly below the stated comparison threshold.
The perturbation margin is
delta minus 2 sigma minus 3 r_j minus 6 R epsilon.
The three chosen allowances each cost at most delta/4. Thus the
fixed credits survive all the designated centers and directions,
with no optimized-tilt compactness assumption.

## The error is proportional to the relevant group mass

The aggregate credits satisfy c_i between zero and e and average at
least J e/N. Their centered vector sums to zero, exactly matching
the sole dependence of the barycentric gradients. The displacement
exists uniquely and has norm at most K_d e/|B|. In particular this
bound uses the mass of this one star, not the total mass outside
the eventual core.

The proper-section continuity assertion is valid for moving normals
and planes: approximation toward an interior section point supplies
the lower Hausdorff inclusion, and compactness supplies the upper
one. All chosen limiting planes are proper, so no supporting-facet
trace enters the derivative. Uniformity follows on their compact
parameter neighborhood. Its error can be fixed arbitrarily small
before selecting theta.

For either sign of the threshold displacement Delta, the signed
coarea integral differs from N Gamma |B| n_i dot v_B by at most

    zeta |B| |Delta| + N Gamma |B| epsilon |v_B|.

The two terms are respectively at most eta e/2. Exact Grunbaum at
the TRUE centroid supplies the starting cap mass. Therefore the
near-facet lower bound is Gamma |B| minus c_i plus its average
minus eta e. Adding the actual endpoint credits proves the stated
alpha e gain. There is no uncharged additive Hausdorff error, and
no Hausdorff-error/e rate is being assumed even when e is tiny.

For clarity, actual unit normals within epsilon/sqrt(d) of
n_i/|n_i| are among the proved functional perturbations: multiply
the cap by |n_i| and write its gradient as n_i+a. The remaining
unit normals form a compact set away from all simplex equality
directions. Their fixed positive centroid-cap gap pays alpha e
once theta is small. A zero continuous normal contains the whole
middle fiber. Thus the local claim covers every ambient orientation,
including the vertical boundary-mass case. All these constants
depend only on d; the number of pairs does not enter.

## Actual fibers, parity, and the final budget

For every nonempty outer fiber, including a zero-volume one, pairing
it with its same-parity positive core fiber puts a translated
half-copy of that core fiber at their integer midpoint. Its volume
is at least 2^(-d) m, greater than the total permitted outer volume.
The midpoint must therefore be a core point. The formula p=2w-v
is unique: parity first determines v and then w. Within a target
group the partners are distinct and none is the target itself.
Hence the local star sum counts distinct actual fibers, once each.

An ambient affine threshold has exactly opposite offsets on each
such pair because their bases average to the target base. The
local lemma allows arbitrary offsets, so simultaneous compatibility
with the one actual integer normal imposes no extra assumption.

Failure of the desired target implies D(K_w)V_w below that target
for every core w, since the ordinary maximum is attained and its
point belongs to the actual fiber. Summing the volume upper bounds
with one minimum volume retained gives max V_w less than m+E and
D(K_w) less than Gamma(1+E/m), with no factor depending on 2^n.
Thus every positive target group satisfies the same local theta
conditions; a group of mass zero uses its ordinary centroid.

The average of the resulting L actual-point lower bounds is

    [Gamma sum_w V_w + alpha E]/L,

which strictly exceeds the desired target when E is positive,
because alpha exceeds Gamma. This averages guarantees for different
candidate points; it does not charge the same cap repeatedly.
The case E=0 follows from a largest core fiber directly. Parallel
translation to a through-point cap handles every containing closed
halfspace, and zero-volume fibers never create an extra positive
source charge.

The conclusion is therefore the stated restricted full OC theorem
with a positive dimension-only rho_d, independent of n. Its
nonconstructive dependence is solely through ordinary compactness
and simplex rigidity. It does not establish the small-outside-mass
hypothesis for arbitrary mixed convex bodies.
